title: HANDLOOM PRODUCER COMPANIES
body_text:
Under National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) need based financial support is provided for various interventions like upgraded looms & accessories, construction of worksheds, lighting units, product & design development etc. State/UT-wise details of upgraded looms & accessories, worksheds constructed, lighting units provided under NHDP across the country during last three years are given below.
The Government promotes the formation and strengthening of Handloom Producer Companies (HPCs) as a key institutional mechanism for organizing handloom weavers into professionally managed, member-owned enterprises. 237 Handloom Producer Companies are formed under NHDP during 2020-21 to 2025-26.
Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme is a component of National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) to provide adequate and timely assistance from the Banks/financial institutions to the handloom sector to meet their credit requirement for term loan & working capital in a flexible and cost-effective manner across the country. Margin money assistance is provided @ 20% of loan amount subject to maximum of Rs.25, 000/- to individual handloom weaver/weaver entrepreneur and @ 20% of loan amount subject to maximum of Rs.20.00 lakh (@ Rs.2.00 lakh for every 100 weaver/worker) to handloom organization. However, only handloom organizations are eligible for getting loans at concessional interest rate of 6% for a period of 3 years subject to interest subvention capped up to 7% by the GoI. Credit guarantee fee on loan to handloom organization only is also provided for a period of 3 years.
For timely disbursal of financial assistances i.e. Margin money, Interest Subsidy and Credit Guarantee Fee by participating banks, a centralized online claim disbursement system “Handloom Weaver Mudra Portal” has been developed in association with Punjab National Bank. Margin money is transferred directly to the loan account of beneficiaries and interest subsidy is transferred directly to concerned banks through the Portal.
For availing loan under the scheme, eligible handloom weaver/worker is required to approach participating bank concerned with the filled-up application and submit it in the bank with necessary documents. It is for the bank concerned to satisfy itself with the eligibility of the applicant for grant of loan to the beneficiary. State-wise number of loan and amount of loan sanctioned under Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme under NHDP during 2021-22 to 2026-27 (up to 30.06.2026) is given below.

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Ministry of Textiles detailed support provided under the National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP), including 237 Handloom Producer Companies formed between 2020-21 and 2025-26, and state-wise data on upgraded looms, worksheds, and lighting units provided from 2021-22 to 2025-26. It also gave state-wise loan sanction data under the Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme from 2021-22 to 2026-27 (up to 30.06.2026), highlighting margin money, interest subvention, and credit guarantee fee support, along with the Handloom Weaver Mudra Portal developed with Punjab National Bank for centralized claim disbursement.
enrichment.context:
The NHDP is a central sector scheme aimed at holistic development of the handloom sector by providing support for raw materials, design inputs, technology upgradation, marketing, and welfare of weavers, most of whom are in the unorganized sector and economically vulnerable. Handloom Producer Companies represent an institutional innovation to help weavers move from fragmented individual production to collective, professionally managed enterprises, improving bargaining power, access to markets, and economies of scale—similar in spirit to Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) in agriculture.

The Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA component addresses a chronic problem in the handloom sector: poor access to formal credit due to weavers' small scale, lack of collateral, and seasonal income. By offering margin money subsidies and interest subvention, the scheme tries to de-risk lending for banks while making credit affordable for weavers. The data shows significant regional concentration of both loans and physical infrastructure support (e.g., Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Manipur, Karnataka, Kerala lead in various indicators), reflecting the geographic concentration of India's handloom industry, which is otherwise under strain from powerloom competition, synthetic fabric substitution, and declining traditional weaver populations.

prelims_questions.question: The National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) is implemented under which Ministry of the Government of India?
options: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that NHDP, including its components like Handloom Producer Companies and the Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme, is implemented by the Ministry of Textiles.

prelims_questions.question: Under the Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme, which of the following statements is correct regarding margin money assistance?
options: Only handloom organizations are eligible for margin money assistance
Individual handloom weavers can get margin money up to a maximum of Rs. 25,000
Margin money is capped at Rs. 2 lakh per individual weaver
Margin money assistance is fixed at 10% of the loan amount for all beneficiaries
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, margin money assistance is provided at 20% of the loan amount subject to a maximum of Rs. 25,000 to an individual handloom weaver/weaver entrepreneur.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of Producer Companies as an institutional mechanism for organizing India's handloom weavers. What challenges do such collectives face and how can government schemes address them?

mains_questions.question: Access to formal credit remains a major constraint for India's handloom sector. Critically examine the design and effectiveness of the Concessional Credit/Weaver MUDRA Scheme in addressing this challenge.
